comment.comment:
AI agents spending money autonomously is a massive opportunity. Securing those transactions could be just as big. That’s why $WORM caught my attention. Agent Wormhole is building protection against malicious instructions, tampered agent configs and payments that don’t match what an agent was actually quoted. Its tools include open-source config protection, token metadata attestations and an x402 payment guard. (agentwormhole.com)

The token connection is what makes this interesting: the project says protection fees fund $WORM buybacks and burns. Its dashboard reports over 37.6M tokens burned—roughly 3.76% of supply—with $14.4K spent on buybacks. Early numbers, but a concrete mechanism for connecting usage to the token.

There’s also an external code review: zauth reports 83 findings resolved, one withdrawn and zero left open within the reviewed scope. That matters when security is the product. (zauth.inc)

My bull case is simple: as agents gain access to more money, checking what they read, sign and send becomes increasingly valuable. If WORM earns integrations and recurring paid usage, that could feed sustained buybacks.

Adoption still has to scale. But security infrastructure with a usage-funded burn? That’s a thesis I can get fucking bullish on

$Worm is the underlying security layer for the RH chain’s AI Agent sector—the security moat for AI Agents~

It’s a foundational tool built specifically to protect AI Agents doing automated trading, intercepting malicious instructions hidden in configs and preventing the AI from getting tricked into making random transfers or buying coins~

Its security logic: when hackers send configs with traps, $WORM acts as the AI’s security inspector, screening out and blocking malicious code. Before the AI makes a payment, it checks the transaction quote and blocks it immediately if anything looks off. It adds a verification stamp to project info; if the content is tampered with, the verification instantly becomes invalid, stopping the AI from carrying out dangerous operations~

For AI automated micropayments like x402 in the ecosystem, all the fees generated by Wormbook are used for buybacks and burns, and 4.37% has already been burned. RH is now pushing hard into AI automated trading, and security is a must-have for this sector~
